title: NEVER GIVE UP: The Adam Wardzinski Story (FULL MOVIE)
description:
From a young Polish grappler with a dream to one of the most respected figures in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Adam Wardziński's journey is a story of obsession, perseverance, and the relentless pursuit of something greater than himself.

For years, Adam stood outside the traditional power centers of jiu-jitsu, carving his own path from Poland to the world's biggest stages. While others followed established systems, Adam developed a style uniquely his own, an unpredictable, pressure-filled game built around creativity, intelligence, and an almost obsessive understanding of the art.

But his rise was never simply about competition.

Behind the medals, the victories, and the countless hours spent on the mats is a husband, a father, a teacher, and a man deeply connected to the people and places that shaped him. His pursuit of greatness exists alongside the responsibilities of family, the weight of representing his country, and the question of what it truly means to dedicate a life to a craft.

Through intimate access to Adam's life, training, family, and career, the film traces his extraordinary ascent from a young Polish jiu-jitsu practitioner to the pinnacle of the sport.

This is not simply the story of how Adam Wardziński became a champion.

It is the story of how one man forged his own path and, in doing so, helped put Polish jiu-jitsu on the world stage.

title: 2026 Polaris 37
description:
On June 6 in Dublin, Ireland, Polaris returns with one of its most ambitious events yet as Team Polaris takes on the powerhouse squad from BJJ Stars.

Representing Brazil, BJJ Stars arrives with a roster built from one of the strongest competitive scenes in the sport. BJJ Stars has become synonymous with elite-level talent, showcasing world champions, ADCC veterans, and some of the most dangerous submission hunters on the planet. Their athletes are accustomed to performing on the biggest stages and have built a reputation for delivering action.

Standing opposite them will be the Polaris All Stars, a team assembled from some of the promotion's most accomplished and recognizable athletes. Polaris has spent years cultivating talent across Europe and beyond, creating a roster capable of competing with anyone in the world. Now they face perhaps their toughest test to date.

Ethan Crelinsten of Simple Man Martial Arts is back to defend his Polaris lightweight title, this time against an unexpected contender. Shaï is a brown belt who has had impressive showings in ADCC Trials competition and now he gets his shot against a proven talent like Crelinsten. Ethan has been having world class success for years now and typically does his best work at 155lbs. This will be Ethan's first action since CJI 2. title: Inside of East Austin Jiu-Jitsu Parlor — one of the hidden gems of Austin, TX🔥
This Jiu-Jitsu Gym Brings East Austin Culture To Life | East Austin Jiu-Jitsu Parlor
description:
Austin, TX is known around the world as the mecca of professional jiu-jitsu. With elite teams like New Wave, B-Team, Six Blades, Fight Factory, and others calling the city home, it’s easy to focus solely on the top of the food chain.

But that’s just one part of the story.

In this episode, we shine a spotlight on East Austin Jiu-Jitsu Parlor — a locally owned gym founded by longtime training partners who were part of the scene long before Austin became a jiu-jitsu hotspot. Their roots trace back to one of the city’s original gyms, East Austin Elite, and their mission today is to build something that blends the soul of Austin with the art of jiu-jitsu.

title: WNO 27: Duarte vs Rodriguez Undercard | Free Live Prelim Matches
description:
Watch the entire #WNO27 card, only on FloGrappling: https://flosports.link/42hcjhP

With a main event many are calling "the biggest match in WNO history," Kaynan Duarte vs. Nick Rodriguez headlines an unforgettable night. These two grapplers were the champions of last year’s biggest tournaments—the ADCC World Championships and the Craig Jones Invitational—and now, they’re set to face off.

Their first two meetings came in the 2019 ADCC World Finals, where Duarte submitted Rodriguez twice, a testament to his dominant style at the time. However, Nick Rodriguez has undergone a dramatic transformation since then. The UFC Fight Pass Invitational headliner’s improvement is undeniable, making this rematch a fresh, high-stakes bout.

description:

The silver anniversary of WNO begins at 8 p.m. ET on Dec. 4 as some of the best no-gi grapplers in the world, and some of the top rising stars in the sport, compete in Houston. title: Natã Tenca Taps 5 Of 6 For Double Gold | IBJJF Pans Day 3 Recap
description:
Nata Tenca took purple belt double gold, defeating six opponents on the day, and tapping five of them with the same straight footlock. The Atos super heavyweight has proven a footlock specialist in his last few years at purple belt, but this was hands down his most dominant performance.
Rafael Gamba of Alliance won the lightweight division with a perfect 100% submission rate in five matches. Gamba is set to return to Brasileiro next month with aspirations for a second consecutive title.
Gregor Gracie student Enzo Silva looked like a veteran all day, winning the medium heavyweight division. He utilized his trademark omoplata to sweep all day, and on several occasions he earned smother submissions from mount.
AOJ's Mateo Cordona showed off his impressive guard passing skills all day to win the middleweight division, picking up three victories, and the gold for his team.
Devin Riley of TLI secured gold in the light featherweight division, earning several submissions including a footlock in the final. This is his second straight IBJJF major gold. He closed out in the final with teammate Quinton Dixon at Euros earlier this year.
Dream Art put three gold medalists on the podium at purple belt today:
João Victor Bolinho at ultra heavyweight, Igor Riberio at heavyweight, and Bruno Costa at featherweight
That puts Dream Art in second place in the team standings as colored belt action concludes, two points behind frontrunner, Alliance.
AOJ sits in third with 41 points.
The black belt divisions start on Saturday morning with the absolute division, which includes names like Gutemberg Pereira, Andy Murasaki and Diego Pato.

ADCC World Champion Giancarlo Bodoni will reignite his rivalry with Lucas 'Hulk' Barbosa at Tezos WNO 21, replacing teammate Gordon Ryan on late notice. 

Now the two will face off in a heavyweight bout on the main card of the event, which will also see the prior co-main event of Pedro Marinho vs Rafael Lovato Jr. for the WNO Light Heavyweight Championship elevated to main event.
Also on the card, Mica Galvao will defend his welterweight strap against the Mayor of Suplex City, Kody Steele. And Diogo 'Baby Shark' Reis will defend his featherweight belt against longtime rival Diego 'Pato' Oliveira.

-ADCC European Trials winner Owen Jones vs ADCC North American Trials silver medalist Dominic Mejia.

title: THE NEW GUARD: Renato Canuto (Full Film)
description:
Originally aired July 27, 2020 on FloGrappling.com.

Meet one of the most exhilarating grapplers of his generation –  Renato Canuto!

With his flashy style and submission focused attitude Renato Canuto burst onto the scene in 2016 by winning the toughest brown belt division at the IBJJF World Championships. He followed it up with a no-gi world title and from there Canuto hasn't slowed down for a second! 

Ever since earning his black belt and moving to Vegas Canuto has been a human highlight machine, racking up the wins in the process. 

In this upcoming thirty minute deep dive documentary you'll see an entirely different side of the arm hunting black belt, from his early days growing up with local legend Marcus 'Buchecha' Almeida to his star making run under the bright lights of New York City at KASAI Pro. Renato Canuto's story is nothing short of remarkable.

title: RONIN: The Year of Keenan Cornelius (Full Film)
description:
Originally airing July 2020, RONIN chronicles the tumultuous season Keenan Cornelius experienced both on and off the mats in the twelve month span of 2019. Told entirely through archive interviews with all the participants, behind the scenes footage and featuring never before heard perspectives about the drama that unfolded in 2019 and beyond.

It was the year Keenan left Atos to forge his own path, the year he went ronin and trained all over the country, the year he took out Meregali and cemented himself as a contender, the year he started a new chapter with Legion Jiu-Jitsu in San Diego, the year he grew even closer to jiu-jitsu after realizing his full potential. It was the Year of Keenan Cornelius.

title: The 22 Best Jiu-Jitsu Submissions of 2022 | FloGrappling
description:
2022 was a wild year for grappling. Between ADCC, the IBJJF circuit, and WNO, we were treated to some of the greatest performances (and finishes) ever seen. 

Every 'best-of' list is sure to have omissions, oversights, and various misgivings. Still, despite this, we felt we had to chronicle what we consider the best submissions from a phenomenal year.  The top six submissions include the FloGrappling award winners and nominees for best submissions.

Watch more here: http://bit.ly/3GKqQ9F

0:00 Elisabeth Clay Earns No-Gi Worlds Gold Over Vanessa Griffith- IBJJF 2022 No-Gi Worlds Gold
0:32 Tommy Langaker finishes a Tarikoplata - IBJJF 2022 World Championships
1:01 Luke Griffith Secures Fastest WNO Submission - WNO: Ryan vs Couch
1:21 Samuel Nagai Hits 18-Second Submission - IBJJF 2022 World Championship
1:49 Sophia Cassella finds the heel hook submission against Jessie Crane- WNO
2:18 Brianna Ste-Marie secures the win with 30 seconds left - ADCC 2022 West Coast Trials
3:07 Izaak Michell becomes the WNX champ after 2hr match against Kyle Chambers- WNX Finale
4:00 Nicholas Meregali finds the armbar in the absolute - IBJJF 2022 World Championships
4:37 Tainan Dalpra finishes Roberto Jimenez With A Triangle - IBJJF 2022 Pan Championships
5:04 Mayssa Bastos Secures Third Europeans Title With Armbar Submission - IBJJF 2022 European Championships
5:27 Francisco Lo's Insane Flying Triangle - IBJJF 2022 No-Gi Worlds
5:45 Ffion Davies finds the strangle submission -ADCC 2022 World Championships
6:22 Gordon Ryan Secures 10-Second Submission over Roosevelt Sousa - ADCC 2022 World Championships
6:49 Isaac Doederlein submits Samuel Nagai With Brutal Footlock - IBJJF 2022 World Championships
7:08 Maria Malyjasiak Captures Pans Gold With From The Crucifix - IBJJF 2022 Pans
7:45 Kade Ruotolo Submits Mica Galvao In the Final - ADCC 2022 World Championships
8:08 Diego Pato Z. Submits Kennedy With Z-Lock - ADCC 2022 World Championships
8:24 J-Rod Submits Colvin With A Buggy Choke - ADCC 2022 West Coast Trials
9:09 Mica Galvao Hits Coyote Armlock - ADCC 2022 South American Trials
9:30 Josh Cisneros Submits Gianni Grippo- ADCC 2022 West Coast Trials
9:55 Gordon Ryan submits Andre Galvao - ADCC 2022 World Championships
10:42 Haisam Rida Submits Cyborg - ADCC 2022 World Championships

title: Kaynan Duarte's No-Gi Pans Reverse Triangle Highlight
description:
2022 IBJJF No-Gi Pans: https://flosports.link/3UQIdfl

Kaynan Duarte unveiled a new weapon at the No-Gi Pans, a highly effective triangle from the back. The reverse triangle (aka triangle from the back, or ushiro sankaku in Japanese) is not a common move, but Kaynan hit it no less than four times at No-Gi Pans. 

Look at how he moves from the seatbelt and shifts his hips high. From this position he digs his heel into the crook of the elbow and separates the arm from the upper body. He will adjust his leg position while simultaneously pulling up on the trapped arm. As the pressure of the choke increases he also forces the shoulder into a compromising position, making this an extremely powerful double attack from a position of near absolute control.

title: Craig Jones Changes Division for ADCC 2022 | Grappling Bulletin (Ep. 61)
description:
First it was Garry Tonon, now Craig Jones has announced he's changing divisions, and it promises a seismic shift in the ADCC landscape come September.

As we get closer to every ADCC World Championship event there begins an intense period of drop outs, division switching and more. Competitors get hurt and have to pull out which leads to a flurry of replacements getting called up, but there are always a couple of last-minute division changes. 

We confirmed a big one just last week – Garry Tonon dropping down to 66kg after four editions – 2013, 2015, 2017 and 2019 – of competing at 77kg was very remarkable, but today we can announced the equally-sensational news that Craig Jones has decided to move up in weight to -99kg. 

A silver medallist at 88kg in 2019, Jones has participated in three editions of ADCC in the same weight class but appears ready to make a change in his career as he goes for the elusive gold medal. 

There are a lot of juicy matches waiting for Craig at this weight class. Who wouldn't want to see him against Spriggs, or Nicholas Meregali, or Yuri Simoes, or 2019 champ at +99kg, Kaynan Duarte?

title: Mayssa Bastos & Ana Rodrigues Set To Throwdown At Light-Feather
description:
Mayssa Bastos, the reigning rooster weight champ, and Anna Rodrigues, the returning Light-Featherweight champ  are set to throw down in the second lightest weight category this year at the IBJJF 2022 World Championships.  For her part, Mayssa Bastos remains on track to capture the grand slam (Wins at every major IBJJF); Ana Rodrigues's record also remains unblemished this year on the IBJJF circuit. 

What should happen if they meet? Well, if their 2019 Pans final is any indication, one could say that Ana Rodrigues is the favorite, but the grappling world changes fast, and Mayssa Bastos is not an athlete to count out.  No matter the outcome, we excepted a fire match between these two should it take place.

title: The 21 Best Jiu-Jitsu Submissions of 2021 | FloGrappling
description:
The catalog of phenomenal submissions from 2021 spans well over 200 notable efforts,  but we've narrowed our list down to the top 21 - the crown jewel being the 2021 Submission of the Year Winner Grace Gundrum. 

21 Andy Murasaki triangle vs Gianni Grippo | EUG Promotions 
20 Micael Galvao choke vs Gustavo Telles
19 Rafaela Guedes guillotine vs Kendall Reusing | IBJJF Worlds
18 Gesias JZ Cavalcante "G lock" vs Francisco Cuneo | IBJJF Miami Open
17 Devhonte Johnson anaconda choke vs Fellipe Andrew | IBJJF No-Gi Worlds
16 Nicholas Meregali choke vs Cyborg | IBJJF Worlds
15 Thamara Ferreira toehold vs Elisabeth Clay | F2W
14 Tainan Dalpra choke vs Tommy Langaker | IBJJF Worlds
13 Tye Ruotolo seated arm-triangle vs Dante Leon | WNO
12 Luiza Monteiro armlock vs Nathalie Ribeiro | IBJJF Worlds
11 Derek Reyfield buggy choke vs Rene Sousa | EBI Qualifier
10 Matheus Gabriel 50-50 armbar vs Luan Carvalho | BJJBet
9 Diego "Pato" Oliveira kneebar vs Josh Cisneros | IBJJF Pan No-Gi
8 Fabricio Andrey triangle vs Jamil Hill-Taylor | IBJJF Worlds
7 Tim Spriggs heel hook vs Kaynan | WNO
6 Gordon Ryan triangle vs Vagner Rocha | WNO

title: The Road to ADCC is almost here 🔥 - July 17, featuring World Champions Kaynan Duarte & Matheus Diniz
description:
Kaynan Duarte is a Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt from Pederneiras, Sao Paulo. Born on January 24, 1998, Duarte trains under Andre Galvao and represents the San Diego-based Atos team. He is the 2019 ADCC champion in the +99kg division.

Matheus Diniz is a Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt known for being the 2019 ADCC champion in the +88kg division. Born April 8, 1993 in Uberlandia, a city in Minas Gerais, Brazil, Diniz trains under Marcelo Garcia and represents the New York-based Alliance MGA team.

title: Jiu-Jitsu Is Back: IBJJF Returns With Open Tournaments
description:
The IBJJF Austin Open took place on September 19, 2020 and was the federation's first jiu-jitsu event since prior to the suspension of the IBJJF season in March. Competitors were thrilled to be able to compete once again, the event sold out and reached capacity soon after being announced as the community were excited to return to action. The jiu-jitsu was firing on the blue and yellow mats, with big names, up-and-coming stars, and even an IBJJF Hall of Famer entering the tournament.

title: Grappling Bulletin: No-Gi Worlds Recap Of All The Brand New Champions
description:
Hywel Teague runs through the results of the black belt finals– find out who was most successful at the 2019 IBJJF World No-Gi Championships.

Third time is the charm for the Absolute division winner Victor Hugo. He lost to Cyborg in the semifinal of the ultra-heavyweight division, but submitted him in only 54 seconds in the absolute final– the fastest submission in No-Gi Worlds history. 

Johnny Tama became the first black belt World Champion from Ecuador. He won the lightweight division in thrilling fashion, fighting through a nasty cut to the eyebrow to come back strong and hit a slick rolling attack into the mount. Tama paid the price for the gold medal with blood, sweat and tears – check out his emotional post-match interview to hear what this moment meant to him. 

The Canadian Dante Leon has had a standout year with strong no-gi performances in various superfights and a fourth place finish at ADCC. He cemented his position as a top-ranked black belt with No-Gi Worlds gold, facing off with teammate Jaime Canuto in the final– no closeouts here. We saw one of the most gruesome armbars of the year, here’s hoping Canto recovers soon. 

Talita Alencar won her third World No-Gi Championship title. She emerged top of the competitive featherweight division, beating Heather Raftery and Karen Antunes. This marks a return to form for Talita, who first won this title in 2016. 

Checkmat took three gold medals in the women’s division with Natalie Ribeiro and Vedha Toscano winning their first golds, and Raquel Canuto taking her second World No-Gi title. Their performances– along with another silver and two bronze medals from teammates– helped Checkmat win the Adult Female trophy.  Checkmat also closed out the men’s heavyweight division, with a gentleman’s agreement between Adam Wardzinski and Jackson Sousa in the final. 

Thalison Soares and Hiago George of Cicero Costha both won their first No-Gi Worlds titles continuing the team’s dominance of the lighter weight categories.  

Vinicius Ferreira followed gold at No-Gi Pans with another at No-Gi Worlds, this time with a submission win over Eliot Kelly in the final. 

GF Team and Gracie Barra both won two gold medals in the women’s divisions. Mayssa Bastos and Amanda Canuto won rooster weight and light-feather for GF Team, and Gracie Barra’s Kendall Reusing and Jessica Flowers claimed the super-heavy and absolute titles, sharing the gold and silver in both.  

A number of first-time World Champions were crowned with Alexssandro Sodre of Nova União winning featherweight, Manuel Ribamar taking medium-heavy gold and Talita Nogueira victorious in the heavyweight division.

title: Jessa Khan Promoted To Brown Belt By Gui Mendes
description:
18-year-old Jessa Khan has been training with Gui Mendes since she was 10 years old, and he says that she has the qualities to become a black belt world champion. Hear it from the man himself. 

"It was important for her to do this whole year as a purple belt, now in this new stage she is going to be able to compete against black belts and feel the black belts, it's just exciting and different.

"She's going to be a black belt world champion for sure. I've been around for a long time, and I've seen many people have her skill level but she's very special. She has the combination of both skill and discipline. That's hard to find. For me I'm just glad to be guiding her."

title: Dream Art Part 1: The Jiu-Jitsu Project Turning Colored Belts Into Champions
description:
A new initiative by Alliance could see the former no.1 team in the world reclaim the top of the podium. 

The powerhouse team have put together a project unlike any other seen in jiu-jitsu. 17 athletes– all highly talented blue to brown belts– live and train together in San Paulo, Brazil. 

They eat, sleep and train jiu-jitsu. Their food is cooked for them, they get access to doctors and trainers, and they even get complimentary English classes. Everything is designed for them to become world-class competitors– and ultimately champions– on and off the mat. 

Project supervisor and 2018 IBJJF World champion Isaque Bahiense is himself a product of a social project. He introduces us to the concept. gives us a tour of the house where they live and explains how the athletes were selected. 

“Normally we will choose them from suggestions. We will talk wit them, try to understand their situation. From there the first invitation was to come and stay for 45 days so we can know and understand them better, see how they fit in. 

“We told them before they arrived that we had sponsors to cover one year but the way things are going we want to last for many more years.”

title: Sergio Hernandez: Black Belt Burglar-Basher Making Headlines
description:
Sergio Hernandez, a tattoo artist from San Diego, made headlines when he used his black belt jiu-jitsu skills to tie up an alleged burglar. 

Hernandez– a black belt under Baret Yoshida– ran after, took down and tangled up an alleged burglar at his father's house. He calmly restrained and held the burglar in a mounted triangle until the cops showed up. 

One thing people may not know is that Sergio is also a tattoo artist and has inked the likes of fellow BJJer Jeff Glover.

title: Andre Galvao Announces Retirement From Competition
description:
One of the all-time greatest competitors in jiu-jitsu, Andre Galvao has decided to start a new chapter in his life.

The five-time ADCC champion and six-time IBJJF World champion, who co-founder the powerhouse team Atos, announced his retirement exclusively to FloGrappling. 

"I think this chapter of my life is over. It's sad, but happy at the same time. Sad because I will need to stop doing what I love most," said Galvao.  

"I have nothing to prove to anyone anymore. It's hard for an athlete to announce he needs to stop, you're done, it's over. I have ideas that I planned for my future, there's a lot of things going on at this time in my career." 

Galvao– who is still committed to his 2019 ADCC superfight against Felipe Pena, but will not compete in any other events– will now focus entirely on his role as a mentor and coach for his Atos representatives. 

"I want to make sure they [his team] are not only champions on the mat but that they can overcome challenges and become a better person, living their dream just liked I lived my dream." 

A full documentary chronicling Galvao's experiences in Abu Dhabi will be released at a later date.

title: The Spirit Of BJJ: IBJJF 2017 World Championships
description:

title: Champions in the Sport: The Mendes Bros Story
description:
From the small town of Rio Claro, Brazil, to the top of the Jiu Jitsu world, Champions in the Sport documents the extraordinary journey of brothers Rafael and Gui Mendes - two athletes who redefined what it means to be champions both on and off the mats.

The episode explores their beginnings in the sport, their rise through the ranks to become multiple-time world champions, and the founding of Art of Jiu Jitsu, a global brand that has impacted the next generation of athletes. 

A story of discipline, vision, and transformation, Champions in the Sport captures an exclusive look into two of the sport's most influential athletes.

title: Duck Under Masterclass by Cole Abate (Official Trailer) | Art of Jiu Jitsu | AOJ+
description:
Learn the complete Duck Under guard pass system from Cole Abate in his newest AOJ+ On Demand series. The Duck Under combines pressure and speed, blending the control of traditional passing with the tempo and sharpness of the modern game, allowing the guard passer to dictate the pace of the fight.

Purchase Link: https://aojplus.artofjiujitsu.com/checkout/new?o=p3609027
Learn more about the series: https://artofjiujitsu.com/pages/duck-under-masterclass

The Masterclass includes more than 5+ hours of entries, concepts, transitions, and submissions. Throughout the 40 classes, Cole demonstrates the effectiveness of the position, and how the Duck Under completely neutralizes the guard player by removing their ability to set up sweeps or submissions.

title: Colored Belt Blueprint Masterclass by Cole Abate | AOJ+
description:
Learn more at https://www.artofjiujitsu.com 

The Colored Belt Blueprint is a reflection of Cole's journey through the ranks, beginning with the kids' belts and leading up to competing at the highest levels of the sport and becoming a NOGI World Champion. Cole's story serves as both an inspiration and a guide for practitioners at every stage of their journey. 

The Masterclass series includes 56 technique videos and in-depth interviews, organized by belt level. Cole shares his experience and provides insights into how these techniques contributed to his growth and helped him overcome challenges along the way.

title: Inside the Dark Side of Brazilian Jiu Jitsu: A killing, Abuse, and a Social Project
description:
Craig Jones investigates one of the most serious true crime stories in Brazilian jiu-jitsu.

I expected another famous BJJ coach scandal. What emerged were allegations far more serious than we ever anticipated. 

The man facing these allegations is Melqui Galvão, a Manaus civil police investigator and the coach behind a “miracle” kids BJJ social project celebrated for years.

This film follows three connected stories:
• the 2011 K*****g of Fernando Pontes, an unarmed man, in front of his family
• the use of a social project alleged to have abused children for more than 13 years
• connections to the 2007 M****r of a young mother, Sarah Lima D’Souza — a case in which police reportedly received a note predicting how she would die

Same city. Same protection machine. Same man named across the record.

The project produced world champions, including Mica Galvão. This film draws a hard line: there is no evidence Mica was involved in his father’s alleged crimes. He is treated here as a witness to a childhood he did not choose.

Built from court material, seized phone recordings, national broadcast footage, survivor testimony, and on-record investigation with media, legal, and victim approval before release.

Melqui Galvão’s first instruction hearing: October 20, 2026.

If you’re a journalist, give this the depth it deserves. If you’re not, share it. Noise is how chapters finally close for the people who lived this.

Craig Jones is mostly known for strangling people without pajamas, but while visiting Colombia he made the questionable life decision to put the gi back on and train with some very legit Colombian black belts.

Turns out grips, collars, and lapels don’t stop Craig from doing Craig Jones things.

During this session Craig drops into a Gracie Colombia and rolls multiple rounds with experienced black belts. These guys were incredibly welcoming and gave Craig some great rounds.

This video is the best moments from the session: scrambles, submissions, and Craig trying to remember how gi jiu-jitsu works while being aggressively grabbed by the collar.

Huge thanks to Gracie Colombia and athletes for the rounds and hospitality. High level room, and great people.

If you enjoy high-level Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu training footage, rolling rounds, and watching a professional no-gi menace attempt gi jiu-jitsu, you’re in the right place.

title: Jiu Jitsu is a cult, monetize it. #bteamjiujitsu
The Cult of Brazilian Jiu Jitsu. Gracie to Epstein
description:
Is your jiu-jitsu gym building community… or building control?

In this Craig Jones Business Class, we break down the blueprint behind cult-like gym culture — the incentives, hierarchies, loyalty systems, and power structures that can turn a martial arts academy into something far more dangerous than just a training space.

This video explores:

• Jiu-jitsu gym culture
• Cult mentality in BJJ
• Loyalty vs. accountability
• Belt systems and retention psychology
• Power dynamics in martial arts academies
• Women’s safety in jiu jitsu
• Toxic gym environments
• Leadership without oversight

From founder worship and visual compliance to market isolation, belt-based validation, and internal hierarchy protection — the mechanics are predictable.

And so are the consequences.

Jiu-jitsu is a sport built on physical control, hierarchy, and trust. That kind of capability demands accountability. When loyalty is valued more than truth, and silence is rewarded more than integrity, harm doesn’t disappear — it gets protected.

This isn’t about one gym.
It’s about the blueprint.

If you train at a BJJ academy, run a martial arts gym, or care about the future of jiu-jitsu culture, this conversation matters.

Watch until the end.

Strong communities require accountability.

description:
I trained with Ashton Kutcher back in 2020. He was suffering a rare auto immune disease called Vasculitis. He lost hearing, his vision and his equilibrium. I was allowed to post this footage at the time, everyone criticised him for what appeared to be lower level abilities for a brown belt. I was not allowed to publicly disclose his medical condition of which he since has. 

During this roll he didn't have full control over 50% of his body. Wanted to let you know more of the story before revisiting this archival training footage.

title: Craig Jones Jiu Jitsu Missionary - Ethiopia
description:
Guardian is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to providing underserved youth throughout the world with full access to Brazilian jiu jitsu and its life-changing benefits.

One of their key initiatives is Guardian Ethiopia, a jiu jitsu social project in Addis Ababa where 57 youth - including 27 experiencing homelessness - receive free training, food, clothing, and medical care.

Founded by Leyk Birhanu, Guardian Ethiopia aims to inspire hope and cultivate friendships amongst its youth participants.  The program is supported by Craig Jones, Seth Belisle, the Fair Fight Foundation, and Michael Clark - with training gear donated by Shoyoroll.

Every mat session is more than training. It is a chance to escape crime and despair. It is mentorship and hope. All thanks to people like you who support our mission.

Learn more or support at www.guardiangym.org/ethiopia. Every dollar goes directly to the youth in this program. #jiujitsuforall

description:
Guardian is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to providing underserved youth with full access to Brazilian jiu jitsu and its life-changing benefits.

In Mancora, Peru, where poverty and limited opportunities hold back countless young lives, Guardian has partnered with the Fair Fight Foundation, founded by Seth Belisle and Craig Jones, to create lasting tangible change. Together, we are creating a larger space to expand the Guardian Peru program to enroll over 100 new students, giving them the tools to rewrite their futures.

Every mat session is more than training. It is a chance to escape crime, addiction, and despair. It is mentorship and hope. All possible because of people like you.

Be part of this movement to create opportunities where they are needed most. Learn more and join the fight today by visiting http://fightfoundation.org and http://guardiangym.org Support the Guardian Gym Project https://www.guardiangym.org and the Fair Fight Foundation: https://fightfoundation.com/

description:
Did you see the Quintet documentary yet? If not watch it here now: https://youtu.be/0dx7eqQBz_g 
Merch out now! https://bteamjj.shop // Submeta: https://submeta.io/@bteam

This training session took place at Imanari's gym in Tokyo back in September 2023, just a few days before the B-Team Bulls conquered the Quintet team grappling event. Craig hits a few signature bullshit moves, Nicky Rod dials down the intensity and has a technical roll with Imanari, Jay Rod spazzes out and Nicky Ryan rolls with Imanari for the first time since their superfight back in 2018. 

Masakazu Imanari, born February 10, 1976, is a Japanese mixed martial artist and submission wrestler renowned for his mastery of leg locks, earning him the moniker "Ashikan Judan" or "Leg Lock Master." Imanari's unorthodox style, which emphasizes quick and precise leg attacks, has earned him a reputation as one of the most dangerous submission artists in MMA history. He is credited with popularizing leg locks and inspiring a new generation of submission artists, and is the creator of the infamous "Imanari roll" technique.

The twister is a submission hold in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu (BJJ) that targets the opponent's spine and neck. It is a highly technical and advanced move that requires control over the opponent's body, and it is often used in BJJ competitions and MMA fights. The twister was popularized by Eddie Bravo, an American BJJ practitioner and founder of the 10th Planet Jiu-Jitsu system.

The twister creates a powerful torque on the opponent's spine and neck. The pressure is applied to the neck and spine simultaneously, and the opponent is forced to submit due to the immense pain and discomfort.

The twister is considered a highly effective submission hold, but it is also challenging to execute due to its complexity and the need for precise timing and technique. It is a signature move of the 10th Planet Jiu-Jitsu system and is often taught in advanced BJJ classes and seminars.

A triangle choke is a submission hold in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu (BJJ). It is a technique where one person, the attacker, wraps their legs around the opponent's neck and head, while using their arm to press against the opponent's throat. The goal of the technique is to restrict blood flow to the opponent's brain, causing them to pass out or submit. It is a common technique used in BJJ competition and training, and is considered to be one of the most effective submission holds in grappling. 

In no-gi BJJ, the triangle choke is a powerful and versatile submission. Grapplers will often use the triangle choke as a way to set up other submissions or as a way to sweep their opponent and take a dominant position. In no-gi BJJ, the triangle choke can be applied from a variety of positions, such as the guard, mount, side control, the back, and even from standing. Many fighters will also use the triangle choke in combination with other submissions, such as an armbar or an omoplata, to increase the chances of finishing the match. 

The triangle choke, also known as the sankaku-jime in Japanese, is a traditional technique in Judo and one of the first submissions taught in BJJ. The triangle choke is a fundamental technique in both Judo and BJJ, and it's one of the few techniques that have been consistently used and passed down from the early days of Judo to the present. The triangle choke is a versatile submission hold that can be used from many positions, and it's considered one of the most effective submission holds in ground fighting.

The darce choke is a common submission in no-gi grappling is very similar to an anaconda choke, but the entry is on the opposite side. It functions like an arm-triangle but is usually set up from a front headlock or guillotine grip. It can be set up from the top when passing the guard or from turtle, and can even be set up from the bottom. This choke was named after Joe D'Arce, an American grappler known for using the choke in competitions, although D'Arce was not the inventor of the choke, but he popularized its use in competition. In Brazil the darce choke is called the brabao choke. In BJJ the darce choke is considered a fundamental submission.

Jozef Chen is an 18-year-old grappler of both South African and Taiwanese descent. Jozef Chen took third place at the ADCC Asia & Oceania Trials in Australia in the -77kg division. He won the 2022 IBJJF Pan No-Gi Championship as a purple belt. Jozef Chen submitted Derek Rayfield of 10th Planet on WNO with a Z-lock. 

Kenta Iwamoto is a 25-year-old Japanese grappler from Chiba, Japan. A brown belt in jiu-jitsu representing Igloo, he won the 2022 ADCC Asia & Oceania Trials in the 77kg division, with three submissions in five matches. He is 3-0 in MMA with two submission victories. He last fought MMA on January 23, 2022. Kenta is a two-time ADCC veteran, having twice won Trials at two different weight, competing at ADCC in 2019 at 66kg and 2022 at 77kg.

title: UFC Vet Benson Henderson crazy highlights from the ADCC Arizona Open
description:
The ADCC Arizona Open 2023 took place on August 5th, 2023 and some of the best grapplers from all around the USA were featured in the results. MMA legend Benson Henderson competed in the 83kg weight class but he was unable to make it to the podium, and in the end it was Andy Varela who won that division. Varela wasn’t the only ADCC veteran who decided to enter the tournament either, as the 76kg weight class saw Oliver Taza storm to victory with 4 submissions in 6 wins. His teammate at New Wave Jiu-Jitsu was actually the one walked away with the biggest victory of the day, as Dan Manasoiu won both the over 100kg division and the absolute division.

Across both the brackets that Manasoiu competed in, he won a convincing 11-0 victory on points in his first match before submitting the other 8 opponents he faced. There was other impressive performances elsewhere too, with Deandre Corbe and Ryan Aitken winning gold at under 70kg and under 91kg respectively. Faye Cherrier put on a show in the smallest of the women’s weight classes at under 50kg, winning gold against some really tough opposition. There was only one woman who walked away with two gold medals at the event though, as Alex Enriquez won the absolute and the under 60kg division with 4 submissions in 5 matches. (TEXT FROM JITS MAGAZINE)

title: 16 Year Old Prodigy Wins - Helena Crevar - ADCC Open Costa Mesa
description:
One of the most promising BJJ/Grappling competitors of the new generation has changed BJJ academy. Helena Crevar, known as Helena Jiu Jitsu Girl on Instagram, will train under John Danaher and represent New Wave Jiu Jitsu.
So far, Helena Crevar has trained under the supervision of world champion Hector Vasquez in Las Vegas. The talented teenager trained at Cobrinha BJJ Las Vegas . Helena and her parents moved to Austin to be able to train with one of the best trainers in the world – John Danaher. Her parents are from Serbia and were both professional athletes.

Helena will be 16 in January and in the meantime she has won PAN Kids 6 times . She holds a blue belt in Brazilian Jiu Jitsu, and this year she won the ADCC for teens. In her record, she already has 17 wins at Fight 2 Win galas, where she is the owner of the junior championship belt (she has already defended it four times). Interestingly, on the BJJ Fanatics platform you can already buy several of her instructionals.

The teenager is extremely grateful for the opportunity to train with Danaher and Ryan. We are waiting for the first performances under the banner of New Wave Jiu Jitsu. The support of Helena’s parents is the key to her success, because they left their lives in Las Vegas and moved with their daughter to Austin so that she could train in one of the best teams in the world. And yes, on his Instagram, Gordon Ryan welcomed the young BJJ star.

Helena announced the news on her IG:

“With this post, I’d like to announce that me and my parents just moved to Austin, Texas and that I will be training and competing under @danaherjohn @gordonlovesjiujitsu and the New Wave JiuJitsu team. I’m super grateful for this opportunity and looking forward to represent New Wave!”
 - courtesy of bjjee.com

Now, with the bracket still to come and one of the most stacked fields in Crown history waiting, we followed him through camp as he gets ready for any opponent, any moment.

title: Excellent Advice from Bernardo Faria
description:
Bernardo Faria took the stage for an insightful Jiu-Jitsu Con Talk this year, sharing stories from his early competition career, how he met his business partners, and the journey of building BJJ Fanatics into one of the biggest Jiu-Jitsu instructional platforms in the world.

Bernardo also opened up about how he continues to apply the principles he learned through Jiu-Jitsu to his everyday life, even years after retiring from competition. From pushing forward through extreme adversity to approaching life’s challenges the same way he approached a match, Bernardo explains how Jiu-Jitsu has continued to shape the way he lives.

“Jiu-Jitsu is just the way I live my life.”

Hear the full Jiu-Jitsu Con Talk with Bernardo Faria now on the IBJJF YouTube channel. 🎥🥋

Simple, technical, and extremely effective. Excellent stuff from Malachi! 👊

title: Pawel Jaworski back in action!
description:
Now that No-Gi season is underway, it's great to see Pawel Jaworski back in action. He captured double gold at the Brasileiro No-Gi with a perfect 100% submission rate, showcasing his highly technical and intricate leg lock game throughout the tournament.

Jaworski has already registered for the Pan No-Gi Championship this October as he continues his pursuit of the IBJJF Grand Slam. Keep an eye on one of the most dangerous submission specialists on the No-Gi circuit.

title: The Bushido Code | Jackson Nagai's Road to Gold
description:
For Jackson Nagai, winning wasn't the only goal.

Having spent much of his childhood growing up in Japan before continuing his Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu journey in Brazil and California, Jackson returned to compete at the IBJJF Asian Championship with a mindset rooted in the Bushido Code—the traditional philosophy of discipline, honor, respect, and relentless self-improvement.

This documentary follows Jackson as he returns to the country that shaped him, reflects on the values that continue to guide his life, and battles his way to the top of the podium.

For Jackson, Bushido isn't history—it's a way of life.

🥋 Athlete: Jackson Nagai
🎥 Event: IBJJF Asian Championship
📍 Chiba, Japan

title: Double Gold in Japan 🇯🇵 | India Risby's Dominant Brown Belt Run
description:
Fresh off capturing the IBJJF World Championship in her brown belt debut, India Risby traveled to Japan with one goal: win double gold.

Competing at the IBJJF Asian Championship, the Australian standout put on a dominant performance, submitting every opponent she faced and leaving Japan with gold in both her weight class and the open division.

This short documentary follows India's journey through competition day, her mindset before stepping onto the mats, and the relentless pursuit of finishing every match.

Five fights. Five submissions. Double gold.

🎥 Athlete: India Risby
📍 Chiba, Japan

Double Gold in Japan 🇯🇵 | Oliver Silvestro's Brown Belt Debut
description:
Oliver Silvestro arrived in Japan with one goal: leave with double gold.

Making his brown belt debut, the Australian standout stepped onto the mats at the IBJJF Asian Championship looking to test himself against the world's best. Over six demanding matches, Oliver showcased his evolving game, secured five submissions, and completed an unforgettable run to double gold.

More than a highlight reel, this film follows the journey behind the medals—from the sacrifices made since he first stepped onto the mats as a four-year-old, to the bond with his father and coach, and the mindset that drives him to chase the toughest fights.

This is the story behind Oliver Silvestro's unforgettable performance at the IBJJF Asian Championship in Japan.

🥋 Athlete: Oliver Silvestro
📍 Chiba, Japan

title: From Purple to Brown Belt in 4 Weeks | Hawan's Unbelievable Rise at Worlds
description:
At just 17 years old, Hawan left home to chase a dream that most people his age haven't even started thinking about.

This episode follows his journey through the biggest stage in jiu-jitsu—IBJJF Worlds—as he navigates the pressure, expectations, and responsibility that come with being one of the sport's rising stars.

What makes this story even crazier? Hawan was promoted to purple belt and then earned his brown belt just 4 weeks later.

Beyond the medals and promotions, this episode is about trust, hard work, and the sacrifices required to pursue greatness.

Watch Hawan's full story now.

title: Chasing Gold: Andy Murasaki’s Uncompromising Path to the World Title
description: What does it actually take to stand on top of the podium? In this episode, Elite IBJJF competitor Andy Murasaki breaks down the intense physical, mental, and technical preparation driving his hunt for his first Black Belt World Title. Andy takes us behind the scenes of his grueling camp, from the grueling rounds at AOJ to the meticulous lifestyle adjustments required to beat the best in the world. He opens up about the sacrifices made, the lessons learned from past heartbreaks, and why this year feels different.

title: Will Wilson’s First Black Belt Worlds Has Arrived 🌎🥇
description:
In his first year at black belt, Will Wilson has already captured a European title and earned silver at Pans after an exciting final. He’s made a major statement in the division and now sets his sights on his first black belt World Championship. We can’t wait to watch him chase gold and continue pursuing his dreams!

The IBJJF World Jiu-Jitsu Championship takes place May 28–31 in Long Beach. Watch all matches live on @flograppling.

title: Will this be the year Gutemberg Wins Worlds Gold?
description:
Last year Gutemberg Pereira made two World Championship finals, Ultra-Heavyweight and the Open Class, earning double silver on one of the biggest stages in the sport.

Now he returns to the 2026 Worlds determined to turn those silver medals into his first black belt World title. Will this finally be his year?
The IBJJF World Jiu-Jitsu Championship takes place May 28–31 in Long Beach. Watch all matches live on @flograppling.

title: Tarcisio Santos: The Lightweight Dark Horse For 2026 Worlds? 👀
description:
Tarcisio Santos is quickly emerging as one of the most dangerous dark horses (underdog) in the 2026 IBJJF Lightweight division. Competing constantly throughout the season at major Opens across the U.S., he’s been sharpening his black belt-level game with every match and showing real momentum heading into Worlds.

Still early in his black belt career, but already proving he can hang with top-tier competition, Tarcisio brings pace, pressure, and sharp technical growth at the perfect time.

Will he shock the division and climb to the top of the podium at the 2026 Worlds? It’s looking more and more possible.

The IBJJF World Jiu-Jitsu Championship takes place May 28–31 in Long Beach. Watch all matches live on @flograppling.

title: Lucas Lepri’s story is one of resilience, patience, and relentless determination.
description:
Lucas Lepri’s story is one of resilience, patience, and relentless determination.

A 6X World Champion and Hall of Famer, Lepri’s legacy was not built overnight. After winning his first World title in 2007, he went through seven long years without winning another one. Seven years of falling short. Seven years of refining his game, making adjustments, and continuing to believe in himself when the results were not coming.

Many athletes would have walked away. Lepri kept going.

That persistence eventually led to one of the greatest runs the lightweight division has ever seen. From 2014 to 2019, he captured five more World titles, and cemented himself as one of the greatest lightweights in the history of the sport.

Greatness is not always about immediate success. Sometimes it’s about having the strength to keep showing up until everything finally comes together.

The 2026 Worlds takes place May 28-31 in Long Beach, CA. Don’t miss it!

title: Brasileiros 2026 Early Preview — 7,900 Athletes, Key Matchups & What to Watch
description:
The 2026 Brasileiros is almost here, and this edition is one for the history books. With nearly 8,000 athletes descending on São Paulo from April 24th through May 3rd, the 32nd edition of one of jiu-jitsu's most storied championships is shaping up to be unmissable.

In this episode, we break down everything you need to know heading into the event. The female black belt absolute is generating enormous buzz, and for good reason. All eyes are on a potential final between 19 year old Sarah Galvao and 10X World Champion Gabrieli Pessanha. After their intense rivalry at this year's Europeans and Pans, a third meeting in São Paulo could be the most compelling match of the entire weekend.

Fellipe Andrew returns in a stacked heavyweight division that also features 2026 European champion Leo Ferreira and the Vetoraci brothers. Andy Murasaki makes his black belt debut at Brasileiros in the lightweight division. Meyram returns to major competition at featherweight. And in one of the most anticipated storylines of the weekend, sisters Mia and Ashley Funegra will compete at a major championship together as black belts for the very first time.

We also look at the absolute division, where top ranked Erich Munis headlines a loaded field, and the ultra-heavyweight division, where Gutemberg Pereira returns to face Gabriel Veloso and Seif. On the team side, Alliance is hunting their third consecutive adult male black belt team title, while Atos and the Dream Team look to hold firm at the top of the female division behind Sarah Galvao and Lilian Marchand.

Plus, a look at some of the most exciting color belt prospects to watch and a preview of what's coming next on the IBJJF calendar.

title: Sarah Galvão Makes HISTORY! Lightweight Wins Double Gold at Pans
description:
Sarah Galvão delivered one of the most incredible performances in recent IBJJF history at the Pan Championship.

In a historic run, Galvão captured double gold and shocked the division by winning the open class as a lightweight, something rarely seen at an IBJJF major. Even more impressive, she defeated a super-heavyweight in the open-class final, marking a milestone moment for the sport.

Follow Sarah’s full journey through the Pan Championship as she overcomes the odds, makes history, and cements her place among the sport’s elite.

Don’t miss this inspiring story of grit, skill, and championship mindset.

title: 2026 IBJJF Pans Early Preview | Storylines, Matchups & Interview with AOJ’s Francisco Papasideiro
description:
The 2026 IBJJF Pan Jiu-Jitsu Championships are almost here, and in this episode we take an early look into the storylines heading into one of the most important tournaments of the year.

We discuss the European Champions competing at Pans, athletes competing in their first major championship of 2026, and the matchups that could define the tournament. We also highlight some of the standout performers from the IBJJF Opens so far this season who could make a deep run.

Plus, we sit down with Francisco Papasideiro from AOJ to talk about his tournament success in 2026 and his upcoming plans.

title: José Steve is signed up for the 2026 Pan Championship!
description:
José Steve is signed up for the 2026 Pan Championship at middleweight and ready to chase his first IBJJF black belt major!
Only 2 days left to register! With capacity at 97%, don’t wait, head to ibjjf.com and secure your spot today.

title: World Champion Sam Nagai Enters the 2026 Pan Championship
description:
World Champion Sam Nagai is officially registered for the 2026 Pan Championship and ready to chase another gold medal!
The last time we saw Nagai in action was at the 2025 Asian Championship, where he put on a dominant performance in the lightweight division to win the gold.
Now he returns to compete at featherweight, stepping into one of the most stacked divisions of the tournament.
Only 3 days left to register for the 2026 Pan, sign up at ibjjf.com!

title: Tainan Dalpra: 4 Pan Championships, 0 Losses
description:
The dominance of Tainan Dalpra continues. Dalpra has competed at the black belt Pan Championship four times, and he has never lost.
Now he’s registered for the 2026 Pan Championship for the fifth time, returning to the middleweight division with his sights set on adding yet another IBJJF major to his growing list of accolades.
Dalpra isn’t just winning, he’s building a legacy. One that’s quickly being etched into the history books.
We can’t wait to see him step on the mat once again, push the pace, chase the submission, and continue his reign.
Only 3 days left to register for the 2026 Pan Championship, secure your spot at ibjjf.com!
📅 Dates: March 25–29
📍 Location: Kissimmee, FL

There are only 13 days left to register for the Pan Championship 2026! ⏳ Registration is filling up fast — head over to ibjjf.com to secure your spot today.
📅 Dates: March 24–29
📍 Location: Silver Spurs Arena – Osceola Heritage Park, Kissimmee, FL
Here’s a clip from last year when Tainan Dalpra dominated the middleweight division to take home gold. Will he do it again this year? We’ll find out soon. 🔥

title: Inside the IBJJF Absolute No-Gi Grand Prix | Victor Hugo’s Dominant Return
description:
The IBJJF Absolute No-Gi Grand Prix delivered one of the most exciting events of the year — bringing together rising prospects, elite black belts, and world-class super fights all on one stage.

In this episode, we break down the biggest moments from Costa Mesa, including Victor Hugo’s dominant run to capture the $50,000 Grand Prix prize. From explosive heel hooks and comeback submissions to breakout performances from the next generation, this event showcased the full spectrum of modern jiu-jitsu.

We also discuss standout performances from Helena Crevar, Sarah Galvão, and rising stars across multiple divisions as the 2026 season continues to build momentum toward the biggest championships of the year.

Subscribe for weekly coverage, behind-the-scenes access, and in-depth storytelling from the world of IBJJF and professional jiu-jitsu.

title: World Champions vs New Black Belts | 2026 No-Gi Grand Prix Breakdown
description:
The 2026 Absolute No-Gi Grand Prix is STACKED.

World champions. New black belts. Massive weight disparities. And 11 high-level super fights.

In this episode, we break down the entire 8-man Absolute No-Gi bracket — including:

– Victor Hugo vs the new wave
– Diego Pato jumping into the absolute
– Michael Pixley entering his first GP as a black belt
– Heavyweight clashes and featherweights taking on giants

We also preview all 11 super fights and sit down for an exclusive interview with Helena Craver following her dominant No-Gi Worlds run.

This event has the perfect mix of:
• Experience vs Youth
• Size vs Speed
• Momentum vs Legacy

title: Could we be at the end of Tainans Competition Career?
description:
In an interview at the 2026 Euros, Guilherme Mendes shared some honest thoughts about what the future might look like for Tainan Dalpra, and it’s a perspective that hits a little deeper than results and medals.
“Eventually he will step out, and be by our side leading the team.” Says Mendes. “I don’t know how long it’s going to take, if it’s one more year or two more years, we have not decided yet.”
Right now, Tainan is in what Guilherme calls a rare window: “This is the phase of the career where you get to see the highest level…Only some people get to this level.” Still competing at the very top, while already being talked about as a future leader. That balance between chasing greatness on the mats and preparing for what comes next is something all competitors eventually have to face.
Watch the full IBJJF Film on Tainans run at Euros only on the IBJJF YouTube channel.

title: Leandro Lo is From Another World
description:
Leandro Lo delivered an absolutely spectacular performance at the 2017 Euros, taking home double gold with his incredibly dynamic style that kept opponents constantly guessing. A truly masterful display from the Hall of Famer.
Here’s a clip from an epic showdown with the always-tough Isaque Bahiense on the open-class.
The 2026 Euros begin this Thursday, January 15th, and run through Saturday, January 24th. Watch all the action from all 10 days exclusively on @flograppling.

title: Next Generation on Display at the 2026 Euros | Juvenile Standouts to Watch
description:

Who should we be keeping an eye on this year? Let us know in the comments 👇

title: Dominic Manno is signed up for the European Championships in the Middleweight division
description: Newly promoted brown belt Dominic Manno is signed up for the European Championships in the Middleweight division. He enters a stacked field, looking to carry the momentum from a successful purple belt season into this next chapter. We can’t wait to watch.

title: Tarik Hopstock’s Breakthrough: Middleweight World No-Gi Champion
description: For years, Tarik Hopstock was among the very best in the division, but a World title always remained just out of reach. This year, he finally broke through, capturing middleweight World No-Gi gold. An incredible journey defined by perseverance, resilience, and belief.

title: Tainan Dalpra Chases History at the 2026 European Championships
description:
We’re just two weeks away from the black belt divisions at the 2026 European Championships 🔥 Tainan Dalpra is chasing history as he looks to repeat his success and win all four IBJJF Majors back to back. Can he do it again? We can’t wait to watch it unfold.
Watch all 10 days of the 2026 European Championship exclusively on @flograppling, with every match live-streamed.

title: 2X World No-Gi Champion 🥇 Cassia Moura
description: Cassia Moura is now a 2X World No-Gi Champion. This year, she challenged herself by competing in two different weight classes,and came away with her second world title. Hear what she has to say about the journey.

title: Fernando Paiva Makes His Adult Purple Belt Debut at the 2026 European Championships
description: Fernando Paiva had an incredible juvenile career, capturing titles at nearly every IBJJF major in both Gi and No-Gi. Now, he’s set to make his adult purple belt debut at the 2026 European Championships in the featherweight division. We can’t wait to see him take the next step in his career, it’s going to be epic.

title: Ashlee Funegra on Winning Her First World No-Gi Title | World Champion Reflections
description:
Ashlee Funegra joins her twin sister Mia as a World Champion 🌍🏆
After capturing her first World No-Gi title, Ashlee reflects on what the moment means and the journey it took to get here. Hear what she has to say.

title: Johnny Anderson Takes on a 115-Man Light-Featherweight Division at the 2026 European Championship
description: After a breakthrough run at the 2025 Euros, Johnny Anderson steps into a new challenge. Competing at adult blue belt light-featherweight, he’ll navigate an enormous 115-man division at the 2026 European Championship. A long road to the top, this one should be exciting.

title: Leo Ferreira Returns to the Euros | Chasing Gold at the 2026 European Championship
description:
At last year’s European Championship, Leo Ferreira put together strong performances in both the Open Class and Heavyweight divisions, finishing with double silver medals. Now he’s back, registered for the 2026 Euros and ready to test himself once again against the best in the world.
Will this be the year he reaches the top of the podium?
The 2026 European Championships🇪🇺  take place January 15–24 in Lisbon, Portugal🇵🇹 . Watch all matches live on @flograppling.

title: Diego Pato is Back At the 2026 Euros
description: Last season Diego Pato took home the Grand Slam winning all four IBJJF majors. This year he is already signed up for the Euros in the stacked featherweight division. Will he take time the gold once again? We can’t wait to find out. 🔥🔥🔥

title: World Champion Larissa Campos is back in action for the 2026 Euros
description: Current World Champion Larissa Campos is back in action for the 2026 Euros. She won it last year in impressive fashion, beating some of the best in the featherweight division. Now she’s back and ready to win it again!

title: Kennedy Maciel is locked in and ready to compete at the 2026 European Championship
description: Kennedy Maciel is locked in and ready to compete at the 2026 European Championship! After winning it back in 2024, can he repeat the success this year? We can’t wait to find out

title: Tainan Dalpra is back in action at the 2026 European Championship
description: It’s official, Tainan Dalpra is back in action at the 2026 European Championship. The 3X World Champion is ready to kick off the year with a bang, and we can’t wait to watch.

title: Master Julio Cesar’s Gold Medal Run at the European Championship
description: At last year’s European Championship, Master Julio Cesar captured gold in the Master 7 Heavyweight division. Seeing a red-and-white belt step onto the mats and continue to compete at the highest level was truly inspiring. There’s still time to register for the 2026 European Championship — visit ibjjf.com to sign up today.

title: The legendary Megaton Dias is registered for the 2026 European Championship
description: The legendary Megaton Dias is registered for the 2026 European Championship in the Master 7 Lightweight division. It’s always special watching a true master at work. There are still a few spots left—visit ibjjf.com to register today.

title: Cole Abate Captures His Second World No-Gi Title | Road to Gold
description:
We followed Cole Abate and Julian Espinosa on their journey through the World No-Gi Championship lightweight division. From the early rounds to the biggest stage of the tournament, both athletes navigated a stacked bracket and ultimately found themselves facing each other in the finals.

Watch the full run and relive how these two lightweights earned their place in the World No-Gi final.

title: Cole Abate & Julian Espinosa’s Road to the World No-Gi Lightweight Finals
description:
We followed Cole Abate and Julian Espinosa on their road to the World No-Gi lightweight finals. Two separate paths, one inevitable showdown. Watch how they battled through the bracket to meet in the final.
▶️ Full video on the IBJJF YouTube channel

title: Javier Barter Eyes First World No-Gi Title After Pan Gold!
description: After a stellar performance at Pan No-Gi, Javier Barter is ready to take on the World No-Gi heavyweight division. Will Panama’s rising star claim his first World title? One week away!🇵🇦

title: Ana Mayordomo: Spain’s Rising Star Takes On the European No-Gi Championships
description: Spain’s rising star Ana Mayordomo is making serious waves in the black belt featherweight division. After bursting onto the scene with an incredible run to Pan No-Gi gold, submitting seasoned competitors along the way, we followed her journey through the European No-Gi Championships. Tap in to watch her rise continue! 🇪🇸✨ Full video on the IBJJF YouTube channel.

title: Ana Mayordomo: Spain’s Rising Star Takes On the European No-Gi Championships
description:
We followed Spain’s young rising star Ana Mayordomo on her run at the European No-Gi Championships.
Ana has burst onto the black belt scene in a huge way this year, capturing Pan No-Gi gold in the featherweight division with impressive submissions over seasoned competitors. Now she’s back on the mats in Europe, looking to continue her momentum against some of the best in the division.
Watch her journey, her mindset, and her breakthrough performances as she chases another major title.

title: André Galvão: Why Atos Is a Powerhouse at The Crown
description: "Atos is a powerhouse!" André Galvão shares why his athletes didn’t come to The Crown just to participate, they came to win.

title: Michael Pixley Chases Another Brown Belt Title at the World No-Gi
description: Michael Pixley captured gold at the Pan No-Gi in October, and now he’s aiming for another brown belt title at the World No-Gi. Can he keep the momentum going? It all goes down December 11-13 at the Las Vegas Convention Center.

description: Julian Espinosa is on a roll! With dominant wins at Pan No-Gi and Euro No-Gi earlier this year, he now sets his sights on the World No-Gi and his first lightweight world title. Can he keep the streak alive? We’ll find out next weekend!

title: Inside Mateo Cardona’s Rise | The Crown 2025
description:
Middleweight newcomer Mateo Cardona steps onto the biggest stage of his young black belt career - The Crown 2025

Raised in his father’s academy in Florida and shaped inside the technical crucible of AOJ, Mateo’s path has been anything but ordinary. After dominating the colored belts, including a submission-heavy run at Brown Belt Worlds. He now enters a division filled with champions, veterans, and rising threats.

Guided by IBJJF Hall of Famer Gui Mendes, Mateo sharpens his skills alongside Tainan Dalpra, Cole Abate, Jonatha Alves, and some of the most elite training partners in the world. But stepping into his first black belt season, Mateo isn’t just chasing experience, he’s chasing greatness.

In this episode, Mateo opens up about:

-His upbringing in jiu-jitsu and moving across the country to join AOJ

-The evolution of his game under Gui Mendes

-His expectations heading into The Crown

-What excites him about facing names like Andy Murasaki and Jackson Nagai

-Why he sees this moment as the beginning of his true career

The Crown 2025 — November 23 at the Long Beach Pyramid.
Watch the full episode now on the IBJJF YouTube channel.

title: Maca Rising to the Challenge | Road to The Crown 2025
description:
After a breakout 2025 season, Maria “Maca” Vicentini steps onto one of the toughest stages in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu —The Crown 2025.

Training out of Art of Jiu-Jitsu (AOJ) under Gui Mendes, Maca has transformed into one of the most exciting contenders in the super heavyweight division. With wins at Pans, Brasileiros, and standout performances across major events, she enters The Crown with momentum, confidence, and a clear mission.

But standing at the top of the division is one of the most dominant athletes in modern Jiu-Jitsu: Gabrieli Pessanha.
Maca has faced her once before in a razor-close match and that moment changed everything.

Now she returns to The Crown prepared, evolved, and ready to show she belongs among the best.

In this episode, Maca and Gui share:

-How her 2025 season reshaped her confidence and game

-What she learned from last year’s Crown debut

-How she’s preparing for a division filled with world champions

-Gui’s insight on attacking the challenge of competing against Gabi

-The evolving trust and chemistry between athlete and professor

-Why she feels ready to deliver her best performance yet

📺 Watch now and follow Maria “Maca” Vicentini through AOJ as she sharpens her guard, builds her top game, and prepares for her defining moment at The Crown 2025. 👑

title: Proving It Wasn’t Luck | João Mendes’ Journey to The Crown 2025
description:
Last year, João Mendes shocked the world when he went from the 22nd seed to IBJJF World Champion. Now, the featherweight standout returns to the stage of The Crown 2025 with a point to prove: that his world title was no accident.

Filmed inside Atos HQ in San Diego, this episode  takes you inside João’s training camp as he prepares to face one of the toughest divisions in Jiu-Jitsu, featuring elite names like Kennedy Maciel, Cole Abate, and Adam Wardziński.

With the guidance of IBJJF Hall of Famer André Galvão, João reflects on his journey from underdog to champion — and how every round, every loss, and every hard conversation helped shape the athlete he’s become.

Watch as João opens up about:

-His mindset after winning Worlds as the lowest seed in the bracket

-Training alongside Andy Murasaki and the Atos team in San Diego

-How his first Crown experience changed his confidence and career

His mission to prove that true champions don’t happen by chance, they’re built through years of work.

title: Sarah Steps into the Fire | The Crown 2025
description:
At just six months into her black belt career, Sarah Galvão is stepping onto one of the biggest stages in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu — The Crown 2025.

Filmed inside Atos HQ in San Diego, this episode follows Sarah through her final preparations alongside her parents and coaches, André and Angelica Galvão.

Sarah opens up about her journey from the colored belts to her black belt debut, balancing pressure and passion while training among some of the sport’s best. With a lightweight division stacked with champions like Brianna Ste-Marie, Janaina Lebre, Bianca Basilio, and Elizabeth Clay, she knows exactly what’s ahead — and she’s ready for it.

In this episode, Sarah shares:

-How it feels to earn a Crown invitation only six months after receiving her black belt

-The mindset that keeps her grounded and motivated

-What it means to compete alongside her Atos teammates in every division

-How her parents’ guidance prepared her to finally “hit the bullseye”

📺 Watch now and see how Sarah Galvão is embracing her moment — one fight at a time — on her road to The Crown. 👑

title: Cole Abate: Rebuilding Stronger for The Crown
description:
Filmed inside Art of Jiu-Jitsu Academy in Costa Mesa, California, this episode follows Cole Abate as he prepares for one of the biggest challenges of his young career — The Crown 2025.

After an early career injury and a comeback season filled with gold medals at No-Gi Worlds and Brasileiros, Cole reflects on the lessons that shaped his evolution as a black belt. With unmatched discipline and a student’s mindset, he’s ready to face a stacked featherweight division featuring world champions and rising stars.

Alongside IBJJF Hall of Famer Guilherme Mendes, Cole opens up about:

-How he rebuilt his confidence after injury

-The technical and mental adjustments behind his return to elite form

-What makes the featherweight division the most unpredictable in Jiu-Jitsu

-His vision for long-term consistency and dominance at the top

-AOJ’s philosophy of precision, discipline, and excellence that continues to shape new champions

Gui Mendes breaks down Cole’s growth from prodigy to professional — revealing why his student’s technical understanding is years beyond his age and how AOJ’s relentless approach to improvement is preparing him for The Crown.

📺 Watch now to go behind the scenes with one of Jiu-Jitsu’s brightest young athletes as he takes the next step toward greatness.

title: Maria Alencar is Ready to Show She Belongs With the Best in The World
description:
Atos Jiu-Jitsu’s Maria Alencar had a dream year, winning all four IBJJF majors at brown belt and earning her black belt on the Worlds podium! 🏆 Now she’s stepping into the black belt division to show she belongs with the best! 👊🔥
🎟️ Tickets available now at crownibjjf.com⁠
📅 November 23 | 📍 Long Beach Pyramid⁠
📺 Can’t make it in person? Watch all the action live on @flograppling

title: Igor Tanabe is Excited to Make a Statement at The Crown
description:
🇯🇵 🇧🇷 For years, Igor Tanabe aka "Fat Ninja" was known as one of the most promising color belts in Jiu-Jitsu, winning nearly every major title along the way. After spending time focused on MMA, he made a powerful return at the Asian Championship, looking sharper than ever. The super-heavyweight moves like a lightweight, blending a dynamic guard with a relentless submission style. Now, he’s set to compete in The Crown Presented by FloGrappling’s Heavyweight division! 
🎟️ Tickets available now at crownibjjf.com⁠
📅 November 23 | 📍 Long Beach Pyramid⁠
📺 Can’t make it in person? Watch all the action live on @flograppling

title: Nolan Stuart is Ready to Take on The Crown!
description:
What a year for Nolan Stuart! Pan Champion, Worlds silver medalist, and the #3 ranked Super-Heavyweight in the world. Now he’s moving down to Heavyweight to battle for The Crown Presented by FloGrappling! This one’s going to be fire 🔥
🎟️ Tickets available now at crownibjjf.com⁠
📅 November 23 | 📍 Long Beach Pyramid⁠
📺 Can’t make it in person? Watch all the action live on @flograppling

title: João “Bisnaga” is no Longer The Underdog
description:
João “Bisnaga” shocked the world this year. As the 20th seed in the featherweight division, he had to face the best of the best in every round, and still came out on top, winning the World title in one of the toughest divisions of the tournament. No one’s counting him out anymore! He’s now been invited to The Crown Presented by FloGrappling and is ready to keep the momentum rolling to finish the year strong. Can he do it again? 👑🔥
📅 November 23 | 📍 Long Beach Pyramid⁠
🎟️ Tickets available now at crownibjjf.com⁠
📺 Can’t make it in person? Watch all the action live on @flograppling

title: José Steve is Ready for The Crown
description:
🇧🇪 José Steve had an incredible brown belt season in 2025, capturing gold at the Worlds, Brasileiro, and Europeans. That’s how he earned his spot at The Crown Presented by FloGrappling 👑 . They call him “The Ice Man”🥶  for a reason, his stone-cold composure never breaks, no matter the situation. Just look at this clip, where he stays calm even while caught in a fully locked knee-bar. We can’t wait to see how he performs against some of the best black belts in the world. 
📅 November 23 | 📍 Long Beach Pyramid⁠
🎟️ Tickets available now at crownibjjf.com⁠

title: Defending The Crown: Andy Murasaki’s Journey to Greatness at Atos HQ
description:
Fresh off his 2024 triumph, Andy Murasaki returns to defend his title at The Crown 2025, one of the most prestigious events in Jiu-Jitsu.

Filmed at Atos HQ in San Diego, this episode takes you inside Andy’s world — where discipline, precision, and daily grind shape a champion. Alongside insights from IBJJF Hall of Famer André Galvão, we follow Andy’s preparation, mindset, and evolution as he gets ready to face a new generation of hungry black belts in the middleweight division.

Watch as Andy reflects on:

-His intense training sessions at Atos HQ leading up to The Crown

-Learning from battles against world-class opponents like Pedro Maia and Jackson Nagai

-The lessons behind last year’s victory — and his mission to win the right way this time

-How Atos’ champion culture, led by André Galvão, continues to forge the next era of elite Jiu-Jitsu athletes

This is more than training — it’s a look at what it takes to defend The Crown.

📺 Watch now and go behind the scenes with one of Jiu-Jitsu’s most technical and disciplined champions.

title: Rubens “Cobrinha” Charles on Jalen “The Future” Fonacier | IBJJF Talks
description:
In this episode of IBJJF Talks, Hall of Famer Rubens “Cobrinha” Charles opens up about coaching one of Jiu-Jitsu’s brightest rising stars — Jalen “The Future” Fonacier — to his first IBJJF World Championship at just 19 years old.

Cobrinha shares rare insight into Jalen’s journey from kid competitor to black belt champion, his unmatched discipline, and how he’s redefining what it means to be a modern athlete — balancing academics and elite performance at the same time.

Watch as Cobrinha discusses:

-Jalen’s training camp and mindset leading up to Worlds

-How he “broke the rule” by proving you can succeed in both school and Jiu-Jitsu

-What sets Jalen apart as a once-in-a-generation competitor

-Lessons in discipline, resilience, and leadership that Cobrinha learned throughout his own Hall of Fame career

-The philosophy behind Alliance’s 15 World Team Titles and building champions for life

-Jalen’s story is more than just about winning gold — it’s about focus, humility, and the mindset that defines true greatness.

📺 Watch now and hear how Rubens Cobrinha Charles is shaping the next era of Jiu-Jitsu champions.

title: Sarah Galvão: From Dream Team to Black Belt | Full Interview
description:
At just 18 years old, Sarah Galvão has already built a résumé that most athletes can only dream of:

-Double gold at Europeans and Brasileiros

-Gold at Pans and Worlds as a brown belt

-And now, her promotion to black belt on the biggest stage in Jiu-Jitsu.

In this exclusive 27-minute interview, Sarah reflects on her journey:

-Growing up as the daughter of André and Angelica Galvão

-How the Dream Team of young female athletes shaped her success

-Facing challenges in the open class and her rivalry match with Helena

-The emotional moment of receiving her black belt after Worlds

-Her vision for inspiring the next generation of women in Jiu-Jitsu

Sarah isn’t just chasing titles — she’s determined to leave a legacy in the sport, inside and outside the competition mats.

title: João “Bisnaga” Mendes: From Underdog to 2025 Featherweight World Champion | Full Interview
description:
From his first days on the mats in Brazil to standing atop the podium as the 2025 IBJJF Featherweight World Champion, João “Bisnaga” Mendes shares his inspiring journey.

In this exclusive 24-minute interview, Bisnaga opens up about:

How his father introduced him to Jiu-Jitsu and his early struggles competing against bigger, older athletes

The turning point of joining Atos HQ under André Galvão

Breakthrough moments at The Crown and against some of the toughest names in the featherweight division

Overcoming 7 years of challenges as a black belt before finally achieving his dream of becoming World Champion

What it means to win in one of the deepest and most unpredictable divisions in Jiu-Jitsu

Featherweight has crowned 9 different champions in the last 9 years, and in 2025, João Mendes proved that persistence, belief, and relentless training can turn dreams into gold.

📺 Watch now and hear the story behind one of the most inspiring championship runs in IBJJF history.

title: Angelica Galvão on Building the Atos Women’s Dream Team & Her Journey with André
description:
In this episode of IBJJF Talks, we sit down with Angelica Galvão, leader, and one of the head coaches behind the powerhouse Atos women’s team, also known as the self-proclaimed "Dream Team." Angelica shares her unique journey in jiu-jitsu, how she met her husband André Galvão, and the inspiring story behind the founding of Atos.

🔔 Don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe for more exclusive interviews with the biggest names in jiu-jitsu.

title: Andre Galvão on Atos’ Team Grand Slam, the Dream Team & João Bisnaga’s Big Win | IBJJF Talks
description:
In this episode of IBJJF Talks, we sit down with the legendary Professor Andre Galvão to discuss Atos Jiu-Jitsu’s incredible 2025 season. Galvão breaks down the team’s dominant run to capture the Team Grand Slam title, the rise of the Atos women’s squad, known as the “Dream Team”, and João Bisnaga’s impressive featherweight World title win. He also shares insights into the future of Atos and what’s next for their elite athletes.

🔔 Don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe for more interviews with the biggest names in jiu-jitsu!

description:
In this episode of IBJJF Talks, we sit down with “The General” Fabio Gurgel to discuss Alliance’s monumental 15th team title at the 2025 IBJJF World Championship. Gurgel details how the team battle came down to the wire, with the final matches of the black belt division deciding it all. Rising star Jalen Fonaicer played a crucial role, securing the decisive points to bring home the title.

Gurgel also talks about the evolving leadership of Alliance, including Michael Langhi’s new role as leader of the competition tea,. Langhi’s leadership, alongside Gurgel’s, has been instrumental in the team's continued success and growth as a global powerhouse. Don’t miss this insightful look behind the scenes of one of jiu-jitsu’s most iconic teams.
